title: 10,000 Small Businesses in Salt Lake City: Goldman Sachs
description: Goldman Sachs' 10,000 Small Businesses program in Salt Lake City helps small businesses create jobs and economic opportunity by providing greater access to business education, financial capital, and business support services.

asr.full_text: Catus Enterprises is a thermoform plastic manufacturer. We're a woman owned business based in Salt Lake City. We make products in several different industries from the utility industry, ground transportation, and commercial airlines. I took over on the day-day operation in 2008. We had seven employees, a very small customer base with revenues that were declining year over year. The Goldman Sachs 10,000 Small Businesses Program has given me a network of business owners who are facing the same challenges I am every day. A lot of the forecasting information that we've learned in the financial module has been very helpful. We were looking at our financial results reactively and really not projecting out what the next five years were going to look like. We have already experienced quite a bit of growth. We are expecting to grow by 18% this year. We're shipping internationally, exporting to several different countries, and that's new for us. The Goldman Sachs 10,000 Small Businesses program is unique, it's educational, it betters the community. If I can be a better small business owner, then I can help my employees, and we can grow, and we can provide more jobs, and we can take our company to the next level. Small businesses in Utah are the backbone of our economic expansion. The Goldman Sachs program is going to be an invaluable asset to teach skills to the entrepreneur. It's going to help them grow their business and become successful. It's good for the public, it's good for Utah, it's good for America. Our guiding principle in this country is equality of opportunity. 10,000 small businesses is a big part of that. Bar Tile Roofs is the Evans family legacy. Bar Tile was started by my grandfather. This is a third generation family business. We make the most durable, strongest, longest lasting tile in the market. In about 2007, with the recession, we definitely took a hit. The whole tile roof market was one tenth of what it was in 2005 and 2010. The Goldman Sachs 10,000 Small Business Program was everything I wanted in an MBA, without all the stuff I didn't want. We just found out about some major contracts that we were going to get, and I could apply everything I was learning directly into the business at the time that I was learning it. The most valuable module in the program for me was, it's the people. Being able to harness my ideas of what kind of a culture we wanted to create here. We interact with our employees on a very personal level. We know their families. In Utah everything's about the family. My grandfather if he could see us today he'd be very proud. I never feel better about the prospects of the United States then when I hear a small business person describe their business opportunity, her commitment, and when you see that you begin to be very very secure that the American Dream is secure for another generation. I wish you God's best. AVAILABLE NOW

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it profiles the Goldman Sachs 10,000 Small Businesses program and its business-education and support role. The speakers discuss networking, financial planning, business growth, and employment, while classroom imagery reinforces an educational and documentary context. The mention of financial capital is presented as part of the program description, with no request for payment, credentials, investment participation, or guaranteed return described.
